title: He Dies! the Friend of Sinners Dies
description: He Dies! the Friend of Sinners Dies in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 234 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ's Death and Resurrection”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: He dies! the Friend of sin-ners dies! Lo, Sa-lem's daugh-ters weep a-round! A sol-emn dark-ness veils the skies! A sud-den trem-bling shakes the ground!

lines: He dies! the Friend of sinners dies!
A solemn darkness veils the skies!
A sudden trembling shakes the ground!
Come, saints, and drop a tear or two
For him who groaned beneath your load!
He shed a thousand drops for you —
A thousand drops of richest blood!
Here's love and grief beyond degree;
The Lord of glory dies for men; —
But lo, what sudden joys we see!
The rising Lord forsakes the tomb —
The tomb in vain forbids his rise;
And shout him welcome to the skies!

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
